gaps.title: No emissions targets
gaps.text: The platform repeals CleanBC and never commits to BC's legislated targets (40% below 2007 levels by 2030). Its only climate framing is three 'tests' for climate decisions.

sources.title: B.C.'s Conservative party just won a majority. Here's what it means for the environment

gaps.title: No 30×30 nature protection goal
gaps.text: The platform doesn't mention protecting 30% of lands and waters by 2030. Former leader John Rustad said in 2024 the party would abandon it.

sources.title: B.C.'s Conservative party just won a majority. Here's what it means for the environment

gaps.title: Nothing for renters
gaps.text: None of the housing commitments address renters, rent increases, tenant protections, or non-market and social housing. The housing plan is about speeding up construction and returning density decisions to municipalities.

sources.title: BC Conservative Party platform 2026: Promises by issue

gaps.title: New spending arrives slowly; cuts start day one
gaps.text: The platform's own costing phases in new social spending at 10% of full cost in 2027/28, reaching full cost only in 2030/31. The hiring freeze and consultant cuts start immediately. Watch whether promised supports (disability increase, seniors care, mental health) actually arrive this term.

sources.title: Lorne Doerkson's Plan for a Stronger BC — Appendix B, Table B1

gaps.title: Revenue rests on optimistic growth
gaps.text: The plan pays for $3.5B/yr in tax relief partly by assuming growth of 2.5%, 2.8% and 3.2% (2027–29), above the Finance Ministry's 1.9–2.1% forecast. If growth falls short, the 'no new taxes' pledge leaves spending cuts as the main lever.
